runners_data.name: Douglas Dc
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's hold-up 8yo has been competing over similar trips on good ground (5th at 12f Goodwood recently) but sim-going record at Standard shows just 2 placings from 15 starts — genuine stayer who ideally needs a strong gallop that is unlikely to materialise here; held up and likely to be finishing when it matters.|

runners_data.name: Cezarro
runners_data.note: Ross Burdon's 4yo has placed on AW Standard (2nd at 8f Lingfield) and drops slightly in distance from recent outings; a natural hold-up runner who will appreciate any pace injection, though his shorter-trip AW form makes the 1m4f trip a slight query here.|

runners_data.name: Heart Sign
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Jack Morland on this 3yo who has placed at 10f on Goodwood good ground; visor fitted and competitive at Standard AW over 10f — the step to 12f looks a slight risk given all recent form at shorter trips, but Murphy's ability to find cover and deliver late is a key asset in a sprint-finish scenario.|

runners_data.name: Marinakis
runners_data.note: Robert Stephens' 6yo wears a tongue-strap and carries the best AW Standard sim-going record in the field (2W4P from 15 runs), including wins at 10-12f on Standard surfaces — this is his primary track type, and while his natural rear-rank style is less suited to the likely sprint finish, his track record makes him a serious threat if he can work forward entering the straight.|

runners_data.name: Premier Cru
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's 3yo is lightly exposed over 12f but has been finding little on recent outings (8th-7th-9th in softer conditions); tongue-tie fitted and Standard AW form is thin (0W0P from 5 runs), making it hard to project confidence — suited to a stronger gallop that stretches this field and is unlikely to get it.|

runners_data.name: Maryland Star
runners_data.note: Dean Ivory's 3yo has finished 3rd at 10f on Standard AW but carries a "fades in finish" flag and a poor recent run (0th Goodwood, 10th), suggesting stamina doubts at 1m4f; hood worn and the horse's natural inclination to come off the pace works against him in a race without a genuine pace-maker to run rivals into the ground.|

runners_data.name: Sapphire Dream
runners_data.note: Charlie Clover's 3yo is lightly weighted (OR 45) and has been running over shorter trips (7-8f AW), making 1m4f a significant step up in distance; "fades in finish" flag is damaging in what is likely to be a sprint, and the trainer's 14-day record (0/7) gives no confidence — however, the low weight could help if the race turns farcical.|

runners_data.name: Mister Daydream
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's 5yo has 2nd at 10f on Standard AW and is top-weighted (140lbs), which is notable and worth monitoring for any market moves; recent form shows consecutive 7th placings at 12f Goodwood in good going, and the heavy weight could be enough of a burden in a race that resolves into a sharp sprint.|

runners_data.name: Lunar Power
runners_data.note: Laura Mongan's veteran (8yo, OR 57) has been running over long trips (16-24f) and is clearly a stayer by nature — headgear (p: hood) suggests an attempt to sharpen him up, and he is one of the likelier horses to stride forward early given his prominent tendencies, though his stamina-based profile means he will fade sharply if a genuine sprint develops at the finish.|

runners_data.name: Moonlit Cloud
runners_data.note: Dean Ivory saddles this 8yo (headgear: p) who has placed once from 15 Standard-going runs but has AW experience and prominent tendencies that make him one of the few horses likely to push forward from the start; his recent form (9th-5th-4th on Standard) suggests he is capable of competitive efforts in the right shape, but declining returns as an older horse make it hard to rely on him.|

races.paceDynamic: Every runner in this 11-horse field is classified as a hold-up type, meaning there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse likely to impose a genuine gallop from the outset — the early tempo at Lingfield's 1m4f on the AW is expected to be dawdling, with the field bunching and drifting into a sprint finish off a false pace. The redistribution note flags that Lunar Power, Maryland Star, Moonlit Cloud and several others are genuine prominent or hold-up horses who cannot all find their natural ground in this scenario, though Lunar Power (headgear: p) and Moonlit Cloud (headgear: p) — both experienced AW campaigners — are most likely to push forward and at least ensure some early momentum. With no true pace-maker, the race is likely to be run in a compressed group, with position off the final bend becoming critical and the finish likely to be decided by those able to quicken sharply over the final two furlongs. This race shape heavily favours horses with tactical speed and the ability to produce a late burst from a good position — pure hold-up horses dependent on a true gallop to stretch the field are at a structural disadvantage, and those who can sit handy from midfield and quicken when the sprint develops hold the clearest edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Off Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo remains crawling throughout and the race ignites into a two-furlong dash, compressing the field.
scenarios.body: With no pace-setter to string the field out, the entire group will be close together turning for home, making position off the bend decisive and rewarding horses with raw acceleration rather than stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lunar Power Asserts Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Lunar Power or Moonlit Cloud push forward early and inject enough tempo to stretch the field and reward those who travel prominently.
scenarios.body: A genuine gallop from these AW-experienced campaigners would create a longer run to the line, suiting horses who can settle just behind and sustain their effort rather than sprint.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If a stronger-than-expected gallop is set by the prominent types and the sprint finish fails to materialise, allowing true hold-up runners to pick up ground late.
scenarios.body: Horses like Heart Sign and Cezarro who can travel smoothly and finish through beaten rivals would benefit as the pace stretches the field and creates space for a late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Scrimmage Decides
scenarios.trigger: If the false pace causes interference, bunching and positional battles turning for home that disrupt several fancied runners.
scenarios.body: In a messy finish where the sprint is impeded, the horse who finds the clearest passage soonest wins regardless of style — lower-weighted or fresh rivals benefit from chaos.

watchPoints.text: No confirmed front-runner in a field of 11 hold-up types means the pace could be genuinely suicidal in its slowness — watch whether Lunar Power or Moonlit Cloud stride on from the off, as their decision in the first two furlongs will determine whether this race has any shape at all.

Mister Daydream carries top weight of 140lbs — the heaviest burden in the field — and recent form shows back-to-back 7th placings; watch market moves to gauge whether connections believe he can overcome the weight in what is likely to be a sprint finish.

Maryland Star and Sapphire Dream both carry "fades in finish" flags — in a race that is almost certain to resolve into a late sprint off a false pace, these two are structurally disadvantaged and worth opposing if they are supported in the market.

Heart Sign (visor, Oisin Murphy) steps up to 12f for the first time on AW Standard — watch whether the headgear change and the booking of Murphy signal a planned positional change that could see the 3yo slot in closer to the pace than his hold-up profile suggests.

Marinakis has the strongest AW Standard form in the field (2W4P from 15 runs at 10-12f) — watch his early movement to see whether Luke Morris tries to push him forward from his natural hold-up position, which would significantly alter the race's tactical shape.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div 1)
Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div 2)
Syd Renwick 90th Birthday Handicap

runners_data.name: Artavian
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race, Patrick Chamings-trained and carrying 142lbs, set to dictate over a trip (2m) she has not yet proven at — her sim-going record of 0 wins from 8 starts on similar ground gives pause, but her uncontested role is the dominant tactical factor here; tongue-tie noted.

runners_data.name: Master Dancer
runners_data.note: Veteran 9-year-old whose genuine hold-up style has been pushed into a midfield map slot by the congestion of rear-runners; Richard Bandey's yard has no recent 14-day runners, last ran 23 days ago, and a best recent effort of 3rd on Standard ground is the one relevant form line to respect.

runners_data.name: Break Point
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted at OR 51 and a genuine stayer who won over 2m on AW Standard ground on his most recent outing — his true closer's instinct is compressed into the midfield by the crowded rear, and with Luke Dace's yard 0/4 in the 14-day window there is no fresh stable momentum, but the course-and-distance win is the standout piece of form in the race.

runners_data.name: La Trinite
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old whose five-run recent sequence is all 6th or worse except a second on Good ground at 12f — stepping up markedly in trip from those efforts and, as a natural hold-up horse mapped forward by redistribution, faces a tactical puzzle in a race where she must cover more ground than she would choose to.

runners_data.name: Worlington
runners_data.note: George Boughey's yard arrives with a powerful 7/40 14-day strike rate, and Billy Loughnane pilots the most lightly-weighted 3-year-old in the field (133lbs, OR 63); a recent 12f Goodwood winner and versatile enough in style to sit off the pace and quicken, making him the most dangerous closer if the pace falters — tongue-piece headgear noted.

runners_data.name: Smith
runners_data.note: Oldest horse in the field at 10, carrying the visor for the first time and 49 days off the track; his natural deep hold-up style is redistributed to midfield, and at OR 45 he needs significant improvement to feature at this level — his 1W on Standard ground over 16f is the one relevant form fragment.

runners_data.name: Home Secretary
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's 3-year-old has been progressive at shorter trips but steps up sharply in distance here; visor worn, OR 59, and just one outing on Standard going (finishing 6th at 8f) limits the confidence — a genuine hold-up type who will need things to go perfectly tactically at a first attempt at 2m.

runners_data.name: Femme Fatale
runners_data.note: James Tate's 3-year-old filly with a hood (headgear), last ran 25 days ago and has not run beyond 14f or on Standard AW ground before this assignment; at OR 57 she is lightly campaigned for this trip, and though Hector Crouch rides, the form string (649-85) offers little encouragement at this distance.

runners_data.name: October Surprise
runners_data.note: A 2-year-old on the card marked with a finishing fade flag — a natural hold-up runner redistributed to midfield — who has not raced for 221 days and whose form at 8f on Standard/Good gives no confidence over 2m; Tyler Heard picks up the ride but the layoff and distance are both significant concerns.

races.paceDynamic: Artavian is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of nine over this 2m Lingfield AW trip, and on Standard ground she is expected to dictate an uncontested, controlled gallop from the front — no rival is likely to challenge her for the lead, meaning she sets her own rhythm throughout. Behind her, the bulk of the field are genuine hold-up types (Worlington, Home Secretary, Femme Fatale, Master Dancer, Break Point, La Trinite, Smith, October Surprise), most of whom will need to make ground in the straight from various positions through the field. Because the field contains far more hold-up horses than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, Master Dancer, Break Point, La Trinite, Smith, and October Surprise have been redistributed to midfield — of those, Break Point (recent 2m+ winner) and Master Dancer are most likely to actually occupy mid-to-rear positions, while Worlington, Home Secretary and Femme Fatale are the truest closers with realistic late runs. A lone, unhurried front-runner over 2m on AW Standard ground strongly favours a horse that can sustain the pace from the front or one versatile enough to sit just off it and quicken — pure deep closers face the risk of an insufficient pace injection to reel in a relaxed Artavian.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Artavian Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Artavian is allowed to stride clear and set a measured, sustainable gallop that never quickens enough to compromise her stamina.
scenarios.body: Artavian dictates every yard at a controlled tempo over 2m, conserving energy and kicking clear before the closers can organise a meaningful challenge; at OR 56 and with a proven prominent style this is the textbook scenario for an uncontested lead. The hold-up field will find the pace insufficient to build momentum for a decisive late run, leaving Artavian's advantage intact at the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Artavian's controlled pace is slow enough to allow the field to bunch, enabling a fresher, well-placed hold-up horse to surge late.
scenarios.body: A genuinely slow tempo compresses the field, so a well-handicapped closer who travels comfortably through midfield can find a clear run and overhaul Artavian in the final furlong; Worlington (OR 63, recent winner, George Boughey's yard in 7/40 14-day form) and Home Secretary (OR 59, Sir Mark Prescott handler) have the tactical profiles to exploit this. Break Point also holds claims given his 1-mile-plus AW form, though his redistribution from his natural hold-up position reduces the chance he finds his ideal spot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Artavian sets a frantically slow early pace that causes a mid-race bunching and a cavalry charge finish.
scenarios.body: An unusually slow early gallop draws the whole field into contention before the straight, turning the race into a sprint-for-home at 2m; redistributed hold-up types who manage to sit closer than expected — particularly Break Point (recent 2m AW winner, LR 7d) — could capitalise. However, this scenario relies on horses racing out of their natural positions finding unobstructed runs, which is inherently less reliable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Increases, Front Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Artavian is briefly pressured mid-race by a rival creeping up, causing a fractional increase in tempo that paradoxically stretches the closers.
scenarios.body: An unplanned mid-race injection of pace from Worlington or another rival tracking Artavian strings the field out, burning off the deep closers and leaving only the most versatile travellers in contention; this extreme scenario is low probability given the race shape, but favours Artavian surviving or a prominent-tracking hold-up horse who stayed close throughout. The OR differentials and light weights at the top of the field make this outcome a slim but non-trivial outlier.

watchPoints.text: Worlington's jockey Billy Loughnane is likely to track Artavian from 2nd or 3rd early — watch whether he attempts to make a forward move on the final turn, which would be the clearest signal that Artavian's lead is under threat.

Artavian carries 142lbs as the longest-priced front-runner on a pace-light card — if she is reported to have shown any post-race tiredness or is seen to be struggling from 1m6f onwards, the weight and step up in trip will have taken their toll.

Break Point (LR 7d, 2m AW winner) arrives fresh and is the most proven stayer in the field — watch his early position; if he manages to sit closer than his redistributed midfield slot suggests, he becomes a material danger regardless of the mapped pace shape.

Several horses in this field (Master Dancer, La Trinite, Smith, October Surprise) are all genuine hold-up types compressed into the midfield on the map — traffic and lack of a clear run in the straight is a realistic risk for all of them; jockeys on those runners will need to find gaps early in the home straight.

Home Secretary represents Sir Mark Prescott, whose patient placing operation often targets AW handicaps at this stage of a horse's career — monitor market moves close to post time as Prescott runners at Lingfield frequently attract informed support when the stable targets the race.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Counsel
runners_data.note: Veteran at eight but has won this track and distance on standard AW going, sits close to pace under David Probert, and a course winning run 30 days ago keeps him spot-on; consistent prominent racer who handles this shape well with sim-going stats of four wins and five places from fifteen.|

runners_data.name: Lebron Power
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner for Richard Hannon and Sean Levey, lone leader in this field which is the key tactical lever; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects he's been mapped as prominent in the data but his actual job here is to make the running, and his recent winning form over course and distance gives him strong claims from the front.|

runners_data.name: Nogo's Dream
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over on this six-year-old who shows a pattern of placing without winning on standard AW, with two places from three similar-going runs; travels prominently and is capable of picking up a place but his strike rate in this grade is limited — the powerful booking of Murphy is the angle to note.|

runners_data.name: Hoodie Hoo
runners_data.note: Strong recent form at six furlongs for Charles Hills and Billy Loughnane, including a win and multiple places on turf/standard — genuinely a front-running or prominent type who is likely to find himself further back than ideal because the field is loaded with similar pace profiles; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects this positional compromise.|

runners_data.name: Sandscreendeliverd
runners_data.note: Pat Dobbs partners this four-year-old hold-up horse who has placed well on standard AW going, including two second-place finishes at five furlongs; dropping from 71 OR, lightly campaigned trainer yard, and needs a genuine gallop to land his late effort.|

runners_data.name: Dontspoilasale
runners_data.note: Highly experienced at six furlongs on standard AW with a solid sim-going record (15 from 15 applicable runs), but has been absent 96 days and is another horse whose natural desire to race prominently is compromised in a field already bursting with front-running types — Jim & Suzi Best yard has been quiet (0/9 in 14 days).|

runners_data.name: Michaela's Boy
runners_data.note: The top weight at 144lbs, Robert Cowell's six-year-old holds a recent win at five furlongs on good ground and a placing on standard AW; Luke Morris rides a hold-up horse who needs a competitive pace to reel in rivals, and the sim-going record is modest (one win from six on standard).|

runners_data.name: Havana Blast
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's four-year-old has been placed multiple times on standard AW at five and six furlongs, and Daniel Muscutt takes over with the trainer active (6/25 in 14 days); a prominent racer with decent course profile who is well-positioned to chase the leader if Lebron Power does the donkey work.|

runners_data.name: Law Of Average
runners_data.note: Arrives in form having won two of the last three starts at five furlongs on good/firm, but those came on different surfaces and his standard AW record shows no wins or places from three attempts; Joey Haynes takes over for a small Chelsea Banham yard, and the hold-up style means he needs a proper gallop to utilise his recent momentum.|

races.paceDynamic: Lebron Power is confirmed as the sole front runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure him, he should be able to dictate from the gates and control tempo on this flat Lingfield AW 5f. Counsel and Nogo's Dream will press from a prominent position just behind, while Havana Blast occupies a similar berth, meaning the race is unlikely to be a dawdle but the pace should be sustainable rather than suicidal. The hold-up horses — Michaela's Boy, Sandscreendeliverd and Law Of Average — will need the tempo honest enough to close off a prolonged gallop into the straight. This field contains more prominent-types than the shape can accommodate: Hoodie Hoo and Dontspoilasale are natural front-runners or prominent racers who are likely to be squeezed back into midfield, unable to secure their preferred position, and Lebron Power is the horse most certain to land on the front end. The tactical verdict is clear: a sustainable, controlled pace set by a lone leader on a flat track favours horses racing prominently with enough reserves to sustain their effort — prominent hold-up profiles who can track the leader into the straight are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lebron Power Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Lebron Power breaks well and is allowed to bowl along uncontested at a true but manageable tempo.
scenarios.body: Lebron Power controls the fractions from the front, with Counsel and Nogo's Dream tracking close behind but unable to mount a serious challenge if the leader has conserved energy; horses racing prominently with sound Lingfield AW form are gifted an ideal setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chasers Collar Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pack refuses to let Lebron Power coast and presses him into a genuine gallop, leaving him vulnerable late.
scenarios.body: Counsel or Nogo's Dream, sitting tight on the leader's heels, pounce the moment Lebron Power's stride shortens in the final furlong; both have proven course form on this surface and can sustain their effort over the flat finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field out and create a true run-in for the closers.
scenarios.body: Michaela's Boy or Law Of Average, fresh off recent winning form, use the honest gallop to pick off tiring rivals in the final 100 yards; Sandscreendeliverd also holds claims if the pace truly heats up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos As Crowd Disrupts Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent runners — Hoodie Hoo and Dontspoilasale — scramble for position early and create a messy, uneven tempo.
scenarios.body: An uneven or stop-start gallop over the flat 5f would compress the field and produce a blanket finish where any horse could land a blow; however, because Hoodie Hoo and Dontspoilasale are not their natural role here the scenario requires several horses racing out of character simultaneously, making it the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Lebron Power's gate break is the hinge of the entire race — if he misses the kick or is crowded early, the entire pace map collapses and those prominent chasers like Counsel and Nogo's Dream inherit an unplanned lead they may not want.

Hoodie Hoo and Dontspoilasale are both natural front-runners squeezed into a midfield map position — watch for a scrappy early dash for position between stalls 1-3 that could disrupt the settled gallop Lebron Power needs to control.

Law Of Average's two recent wins came on good or firmer ground; his AW standard record reads 0W0P from three starts — watch whether he travels with the same fluency on this surface before trusting his late run.

Havana Blast's trainer James Fanshawe is in a productive 14-day spell (6/25), and Daniel Muscutt is a strong Lingfield AW jockey — small angles worth monitoring if Havana Blast is prominent through the early stages.

Dontspoilasale returns after a 96-day absence; despite a perfect sim-going record (15/15), that layoff combined with racing out of preferred position makes him one to treat with caution rather than follow blindly.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Solar Edge
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 4yo with strong recent course-and-distance form (1/5f/FIR, 2/5f/STA), handles Standard going well (7/15 sim-going, 1W3P), and Gina Mangan knows this horse; ideally suited to sit on Temple Of Athena's shoulder and pick her off late.

runners_data.name: Accrual
runners_data.note: Best Standard-going record in the field (13/15 sim-going, 3W6P), but a hold-up horse who will need things to go wrong for the pace-setters; hood and ear shields noted, Rossa Ryan a positive booking, yet the race shape offers him little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Tan Rapido
runners_data.note: Genuine strong hold-up runner whose natural rear-of-field position is squeezed out by the volume of closers in this field — recent form shows a string of 7s and 8s on both Good and Standard, and there is little in the data to suggest a turnaround here.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Missile
runners_data.note: A true hold-up performer with headgear (p) who has struggled to hit the frame on Standard (8/15 sim-going, 2W2P); 64 days off the track adds an additional question mark, and being forced wider in the pack rather than settled at the rear does not help.

runners_data.name: Nezeeh
runners_data.note: Worrying profile: no wins or places on similar going (sim-going 2/15, 0W0P), a series of double-digit finishes, and a trainer with no winners from 19 runners in 14 days; even if he gets a clear run from a redistributed midfield position, the raw numbers offer no reason for confidence.

runners_data.name: Mick's Spirit
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has a genuine Standard AW win over 5f (1/5f/STA) and a solid sim-going record (14/15, 3W4P); TV visor retained, and Conrad Allen's stable is quiet, but his best chance comes only if the race degenerates into a sprint finish from the pack.

runners_data.name: Dyrholaey
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner (OR 87) with an outstanding Standard-going record (14/15 sim-going, 5W8P) and a recent win over 6f/STA; hold-up by profile but the class advantage is real, and Harry Vigors (5) claiming 5lb makes the weight attractive — needs luck from his deep position.

runners_data.name: Temple Of Athena
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who is the pace map's pivot; lone leader with only Solar Edge to pressure her, she sets her own terms on a flat track that suits wire-to-wire performances — sim-going is thin (1/12) but that one run produced her only win; STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence in a contested shape.

runners_data.name: Almaty Star
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type with a 1/5f/GOO win and 2/5f/STA placing in recent history, but sim-going on Standard shows 0 wins from 8 attempts (0W5P); back quickly after 14 days and drawn wide — Jack Mitchell's booking is a positive but the race shape does not set him up well.

races.paceDynamic: Temple Of Athena is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only Solar Edge as a genuine prominent type to apply any pressure, she is likely to dictate a controlled, single-file gallop from the off on this flat Lingfield AW 5f. That sustainable pace — unchallenged and self-set — creates a race that rewards the horse sitting closest to the leader off a relaxed tempo, able to quicken from a position of comfort rather than closing ground from deep. The majority of this field — Tan Rapido, Ziggy's Missile, Nezeeh, Mick's Spirit, Dyrholaey, and Almaty Star — are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because there are simply too many for the rear slots, meaning the true back-of-the-field position will be crowded and those runners face a genuine positional disadvantage on a track that rarely rewards late swoops over this trip. The race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace — Solar Edge and Dyrholaey (if he settles closer than mapped) are the primary beneficiaries, while Temple Of Athena's ability to control tempo gives her a material advantage over a field that cannot collectively generate the pressure needed to reel her in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Temple Controls, Wires To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Temple Of Athena breaks cleanly and is allowed to roll along unchallenged at a tempo she sets herself.
scenarios.body: She dictates from the front on a flat, fair surface with no rival capable of burning her off early, and the hold-up pack faces too much ground to make up over only 5f at a sustainable pace. Horses able to track her closely — Solar Edge, Dyrholaey if prominent — are best placed to pounce, but the leader's rhythm is hard to disrupt.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Temple Of Athena sets a pace just brisk enough that a horse tracking closely throughout picks her off in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Solar Edge has excellent recent form at this course and distance and is ideally drawn to sit second, ready to capitalise the moment the leader ties up. Dyrholaey, despite a hold-up profile, has the class (OR 87) and Standard-going record (14/15) to overhaul a weakening leader if he positions himself closer than usual.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Chaos At Start, Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If there is a troubled start or Temple Of Athena fails to stride on, creating a messy crawl and a bunched finish.
scenarios.body: A genuine sprint finish from the pack would compress the field and give hold-up types an uncharacteristic chance, though most here are redistributed into roles they do not naturally fill. Mick's Spirit, who has genuine course-and-distance form (1/5f/STA) and consistent Standard-going returns, becomes a credible threat in a flat-out dash.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swamps Them
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the field strings out and a true closer finds daylight late.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on redistributed hold-up horses actually securing a back position and delivering a late run — a low-probability combination given track bias and race shape. Accrual's record on Standard going (13/15 attempts) gives her the best credentials of the true closers, but the course-and-distance evidence and pace map both work against this materialising.

watchPoints.text: Temple Of Athena's draw and early break are critical — if she is slow away, Solar Edge could steal the rail and the entire pace dynamic reverses, removing the primary scenario.

Dyrholaey is the class runner (OR 87, 5W8P on Standard) but will need a clear passage from a wide hold-up position — a crowded midfield pack of redistributed horses means traffic is a genuine risk in the closing stages.

Almaty Star returned quickly (14 days) and is trained by Robert Cowell alongside Ziggy's Missile — watch for any stable market drift or support that signals which of Cowell's two runners is preferred.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Tan Rapido, Ziggy's Missile, Nezeeh, Mick's Spirit) will all be competing for the same ground in the middle to rear of the pack — any interference or checking between them in the first furlong could affect multiple runners simultaneously.

races.name: Expert Entertainment & Event Solutions Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Follow attheraces On Instagram Handicap

runners_data.name: Wild Rosie
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Chris Dwyer and William Carson with a poor record on similar going (0 wins or places from 6 runs on standard), stepping back up to a mile; nothing in her recent form (off 26 days) suggests she can overcome her modest surface record from the rear.

runners_data.name: Fallacious Promise
runners_data.note: John Butler's filly has placed three times from seven runs on this surface and course, making her the most consistent AW performer in the field; a natural hold-up type who will be shuffled closer to midfield in a small field, which actually suits her better than her true rear preference.

runners_data.name: Action Reaction
runners_data.note: George Boughey's gelding has a headgear note (tongue-tie, blinkers) and Billy Loughnane takes over in the saddle; genuine hold-up horse who has struggled to make an impact in recent outings and faces competition from several others for the same late-running berth, limiting his probability of securing an ideal run.

runners_data.name: Moravian
runners_data.note: Three-race form string is thin (705) and all runs have been at shorter trips of six and seven furlongs; the step to a mile for Gary and Josh Moore's three-year-old is unproven, and as a natural closer in a field stacked with hold-up types, he will find it hard to find daylight from the back.

runners_data.name: Henfield
runners_data.note: Karen Jewell's filly carries a fade-in-finish flag and her recent form figures of 580-98 make grim reading; off 18 days, she has struggled at trips up to ten furlongs on good ground and shows no obvious profile to suggest she reverses these trends, compounding the concern about her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Laurasia
runners_data.note: Laura Mongan runner for Georgia Dobie, last seen 14 days ago finishing fifth on this surface; two of her five runs have been at eight furlongs on standard, so the trip is not new, but she has placed just twice from five tries and is another genuine hold-up type competing for the same limited late-running positions.

runners_data.name: Ruiz
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's gelding is the only horse mapped to the lead, but he is a redistributed prominent type rather than a natural front-runner, carries a fade-in-finish warning, and has recorded double-figure finishes in his last four starts; he sets the pace by default rather than by design, which is a crucial distinction.

runners_data.name: Ernie McCrew
runners_data.note: Returned just three days ago (4th, 7f, STA) and lines up quickly again for JS Moore and Taylor Fisher; has placed once in four runs on standard going and has finished in the frame at seven furlongs on this surface, so a compact sprint finish over a mile could expose stamina questions, but recent activity is a slight positive.

runners_data.name: Whazzimo
runners_data.note: James Ferguson has a strong 14-day record (4/8) and Daniel Muscutt takes the ride; however, all three career starts have been at five and six furlongs, making this mile trip a significant step into the unknown for a hold-up type who already carries a fade-in-finish flag — the trip extension is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Athenian Spirit
runners_data.note: William Knight's filly has shown consistent placed form (four places from ten runs) and is better than her OR of 54 suggests on raw evidence; a natural hold-up horse who has been placed at seven and eight furlongs on standard going, and Hector Crouch's experience of the track could help her secure a more forward position than her true style demands.

races.paceDynamic: Ruiz is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this race, redistributed to the front despite being a natural hold-up type, meaning the pace he sets is likely to be modest and sustainable rather than genuinely pressured — a lone, uncontested gallop around Lingfield's flat polytrack mile. With no genuine front-runner in the field, the tempo is unlikely to be strong enough to string the field out, creating a scenario where the race is run in a compact bunch before a late sprint for home. This race shape strongly favours those who can position handily in the first few lengths behind Ruiz and produce a turn-of-foot in the closing stages — in other words, prominent-to-midfield types with finishing speed. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the pace map can honestly accommodate; Athenian Spirit, Fallacious Promise, Action Reaction, Moravian, Laurasia, and Henfield are all natural hold-up horses shown in midfield precisely because there is no room at the rear — those most likely to actually secure a forward position off a genuine impulse are Athenian Spirit (placed form at the course) and Fallacious Promise (consistent place record on this surface), though even they will be racing partly out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ruiz Dictates, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Ruiz sets a comfortable, uncontested pace and the field settles in a bunch, triggering a late dash from around two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Ruiz controls tempo from the front with no genuine challenger for the lead, keeping fractions even and ensuring the race is not truly run; horses positioned just behind benefit most as the pack quickens together in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If one or two runners push forward to sit prominently behind Ruiz and use that position to get first run entering the straight.
scenarios.body: A horse that tracks the modest pace just off the shoulder of Ruiz can pounce two furlongs out before the hold-up horses have time to organise their challenge; the lack of genuine pace pressure makes this position golden.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slower than expected and the field bunches to such a degree that a wider, sweeping run from the rear becomes viable in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The compressed nature of the race creates a wall of horses that a hold-up runner can skirt around on the outside if the gap opens at the right moment; this scenario is discounted because so many of the ostensible closers are natural hold-up types racing out of role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Ruiz Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Ruiz quickens the pace in the final quarter-mile and the field is slow to react, allowing the pace-setter to steal enough of a buffer to hold on.
scenarios.body: While Ruiz carries a fade-in-finish tag and is a redistributed prominent type rather than a born front-runner, a field this weak in terms of finishing kick could fail to reel him in if the response is sluggish; this remains the least likely outcome given his recent form figures.

watchPoints.text: Ruiz is the accidental pace-setter in this race — watch whether he is actually allowed to stride clear or whether another runner pushes him harder than expected, which would dramatically alter the tempo and favour different profiles.

Whazzimo has never raced beyond six furlongs; if she fades sharply in the closing stages as her fade-in-finish flag suggests, watch whether she obstructs the runs of closers coming from behind her on the inside rail.

Athenian Spirit and Fallacious Promise are both natural hold-up types mapped forward — if both attempt to push up early, they risk burning energy against their instincts and compromising their usual late kick.

Ernie McCrew's quick turnaround (only 3 days since last run) is worth monitoring in the paddock; horses returning this quickly can show fatigue in the closing stages, particularly over a trip they have not convincingly handled.

Georgia Dobie on Laurasia is the least experienced jockey combination in the race — in a compressed, tactical affair where positioning in the bunch is critical, watch how she navigates the early stages from the hold-up position.
